best_for: PC gamers who want to play their games from another room or on the road, on a laptop, Mac, phone or TV, streamed from their own gaming PC running Sunshine.

points.title: Free with no strings
points.text: Moonlight is a GPLv3 community project. The site says there are no ads, bundled services, paid tiers or subscriptions.

points.title: You need a host on your PC
points.text: Moonlight is only the client. On the gaming PC you run Sunshine, the recommended host, or Wolf. NVIDIA's GeForce Experience GameStream is being discontinued, so new setups should use Sunshine.

points.title: Up to 4K, HDR and 120 FPS
points.text: The PC client streams up to 4K with HDR and up to 120 frames per second, with H.264, HEVC and AV1 video and 7.1 surround sound. AV1, YUV 4:4:4 and 10-point touch need a Sunshine host, and AV1 also needs a host GPU that supports it.

points.title: Controllers, mouse and keyboard
points.text: Gamepads work with rumble and motion controls for up to 16 players. Mouse capture suits games, direct mouse control suits desktop use, and shortcuts like Alt+Tab can pass to the host.

points.title: Clients nearly everywhere
points.text: Beyond Windows and Mac there are official clients for Linux, Android, iOS, Apple TV, ChromeOS, Steam Link and Raspberry Pi. Ports for Xbox, Switch, webOS TVs and others come from the community.

points.title: Playing away from home
points.text: Streaming over the internet works with port forwarding, IPv6 or a virtual network such as Tailscale or ZeroTier.

points.title: What this page lists
points.text: Windows builds are machine-wide installers for x64 and Arm64, needing Windows 10 version 1809 or later. The Mac build is universal and needs macOS 13. The Windows listing keeps 20 versions; macOS only the current one. Linux users get Flatpak, Snap or AppImage from the project.
